signals.title: USD/JPY — Hormuz Escalation + Bull Steepener
signals.text: Geopolitical tension in the Strait of Hormuz and a US bull steepener regime (+41bp 2s10s) drive JPY safe-haven demand toward the 157.00 level. JPY COT net short -63.6k creates short-squeeze risk (USD/JPY downside if shorts cover) as USD/JPY trades below its SMA200 (158.07) amid a -2.20 risk reversal downside skew. The next BoJ meeting (mkt: 100% hold priced) is the catalyst for confirming whether domestic data outperformance (ESI +16.1) justifies a hawkish shift.

signals.title: CHF/JPY — G10 Bilateral Theme + Safe Haven Divergence
signals.text: JPY outperformance (+1.252%) vs CHF weakness (-0.704%) creates a 1.956% G10 spread that targets JPY strength in the cross. JPY is capturing safe-haven flows from the Hormuz shipping crisis while CHF lags with a -11.6 ESI and a mildly accommodative real rate of -0.45%. The next BoJ meeting (mkt: 100% hold priced) on 18 Sep determines if this bilateral momentum persists against the JPY carry disadvantage.

signals.title: AUD/USD — Crowded Long Unwind Risk
signals.text: AUD COT LF long +37.9k (72.1% long) creates a crowded-long unwind risk despite the pair closing at 0.7071 above all major SMAs. While the +70bp OIS carry advantage favors AUD, a negative ESI of -11.1 and the RBA's hold bias limit further upside potential. The next RBA meeting (mkt: 100% hold priced) on 11 Aug is the catalyst for resolving the tension between bullish positioning and deteriorating data surprises.

signals.title: EUR/USD — ECB Hike Bias vs Negative COT Sentiment
signals.text: EUR/USD closed at 1.1562 with an ECB hike bias providing support, yet a heavy EUR COT net short of -73.0k (34% long) keeps the pair capped below the SMA200 of 1.1633. The SOFR/ESTR +146bp carry advantage for USD remains a persistent headwind for sustained EUR recovery despite recent soft US payrolls. The next ECB meeting (mkt: 53% hike priced) on 10 Sep determines if the hawkish bias can force a COT short-covering rally.

signals.title: NZD/USD — ESI Outperformance vs Positioning Extremes
signals.text: NZD's G10-leading ESI of +24.4 signals sustained data outperformance that contradicts the extreme net short COT positioning of -30.7k (only 9.7% long). RBNZ holds at 2.5%. The next RBNZ meeting (mkt: 100% hike priced) on 2 Sep is the catalyst for validating this fundamental divergence.
